articles.title: Hackers Used Meta’s AI Support Bot to Seize Instagram Accounts
articles.summary: Microsoft just dropped a record-breaking 200 security patches in one Patch Tuesday, with 36 critical vulns that could ruin your entire month. When Redmond breaks their own records for broken code, you know it's been a particularly creative quarter for the bug hunters.

articles.title: Victory! 702 has Expired!
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually published AWS GovCloud keys and agency secrets on public GitHub because apparently operational security is just a suggestion. Congress is now demanding answers while the cybersecurity agency tries to explain how they got owned by their own people.

articles.title: Yes to California's Bill to Ban Surveillance Pricing
articles.summary: Section 702 surveillance authority has expired, dealing a blow to the surveillance state's warrantless dragnet collection of Americans' communications. Sometimes the system works exactly as intended - by running out of legal authority to spy on us.

articles.title: Claude Fable 5 Doesn't Change the Mythos Security Story
articles.summary: ShinyHunters leveraged an Oracle zero-day to absolutely devastate higher education networks, because apparently university IT security is still stuck in the 1990s. Nothing says 'ivory tower' quite like getting pwned by a known ransomware crew exploiting basic enterprise software.

articles.title: Civil Records for Hundreds of Thousands of Lebanese Could Be Wiped Out By Israel’s Total War
articles.summary: Army whistleblower exposes systematic cover-up of child abuse at military daycare centers, with officials first claiming evidence didn't exist then magically producing it months later. The military-industrial complex protecting itself at the expense of children - shocking absolutely no one who's been paying attention.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Chrome 0-Day, UniFi Exploits, macOS Stealers, VPN Flaw and More
articles.summary: Researchers chained three Microsoft 365 Copilot bugs into 'SearchLeak' - a one-click attack that could exfiltrate emails, calendars, and MFA codes. Because nothing says 'enterprise security' quite like turning your AI assistant into an unwitting data thief.

articles.title: Security Affairs newsletter Round 581 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION
articles.summary: Attackers compromised trusted WordPress plugin scripts from PushEngage, OptinMonster, and TrustPulse to plant backdoors on countless sites. Supply chain attacks continue proving that trusting third-party code is basically digital Russian roulette with extra steps.

articles.title: Privacy own-goal: World Cup blunder leaks Lionel Messi’s passport details
articles.summary: Iranian hackers penetrated California water systems and issued a 'warning' to Trump about their ability to disrupt drinking supplies. Critical infrastructure security remains a dumpster fire, but at least the hackers are being polite about their capabilities.

articles.title: Oracle Addresses PeopleSoft Vulnerability Amid Reports of Zero-Day Attacks
articles.summary: Oracle finally acknowledged a security flaw that cybercriminals have been actively exploiting in mass-hacking campaigns against 100+ organizations. Nothing quite like Oracle's legendary transparency - acknowledging vulnerabilities only after the entire internet gets pwned.

articles.title: CISA BOD 26-04: Frequently asked questions about the new risk-based patching directive
articles.summary: Oracle released mitigations for CVE-2026-35273 after ShinyHunters went on a PeopleSoft rampage, but won't confirm if it was actually a zero-day. Corporate doublespeak at its finest - 'we fixed something that may or may not have been broken in the way you think it was.'
